requirements.statement: When a new return code is set ('S'), if it is greater than the highest code recorded so far (RC-HIGHEST-CODE) it becomes the new highest code; otherwise the highest code is kept. In both cases the current code becomes the new code. The highest code is held in the caller's request area, so it persists only as long as the caller keeps that area.
When a new return code is set, the system classifies it: 0 is SUCCESS ('S'), 1 to 4 is WARNING ('W'), 5 to 8 is ERROR ('E') and any other value is SEVERE ('F'). The response code is then set to 0.

SET request classifies the new code: 0 success, 1-4 warning, 5-8 error, anything else severe, and keeps the highest code seen in the caller's area (state lives in the caller-supplied RC-REQUEST-AREA, not in this program).

limitations.limitation: a requirements:<ids> selector accepts and filters only items of kind "requirement": runtime requirement IDs are rejected (so RT-RTNCDE00-001 could only be included implicitly), and every runtime requirement, file-operation and data-record item of the unit is included
limitations.effect: blocking items outside the candidate are in the subset scope: RT-RTNCDE00-002, RT-RTNCDE00-003
limitations.minimal_policy_change: let the requirements selector also select runtime requirements by ID (RT-*), and include the unit's data contracts only when a selected item references their fields; everything selected still needs evidence and a signature

limitations.limitation: a unit-level decision with no affected requirements applies to every scope on the unit, even when the selected behaviour never reaches what it concerns
limitations.effect: decisions not reached by the candidate still block it: DR-F2-0011-001
limitations.minimal_policy_change: apply such a decision to a requirements subset only when a selected item reaches its subject (the same semantic edge G2 now computes), and list it as a reviewable, traceable deferral otherwise. It is never excluded or resolved implicitly, and it still applies to the program scope.
